strengths: The paper proposes a novel and intuitively appealing connection between KV-cache compression and supervision for continuous latent reasoning. Matching compressed teacher KV trajectories provides a richer signal than endpoint-only distillation.
The method is evaluated on three backbone sizes/families and compared with several relevant latent-reasoning baselines, including CODI, PCCoT, Coconut, and iCoT.
KAVA delivers substantial in-distribution gains over CODI/PCCoT in several configurations, particularly for Qwen-0.5B and the natural-language GSM8K training variant.

The paper includes useful ablations on eviction criteria, loss type and coefficient, latent-token count, Jacobi iterations, projection, and trace preprocessing, as well as preliminary analyses of latent-token decoding and teacher-student KV similarity.
The presentation is generally clear, and the main datasets, training hyperparameters, and public model checkpoints are identified.
weaknesses: The central claim that KAVA consistently outperforms strong latent baselines is not supported by Table 1. For example, CODI is better on Llama-1B GSM8K-Hard and SVAMP under GSM8K-AUG, and on Llama-3B SVAMP under GSM8K-AUG-NL. Improvements are therefore model- and benchmark-dependent.

The efficiency evidence is inadequate for the deployment claims. Counting forward passes treats a Jacobi pass over 24 latent positions as comparable to a cached autoregressive one-token pass. No wall-clock latency, FLOPs, peak memory, KV-cache size, or throughput measurements are reported.

Evaluation is confined to GSM8K-derived training data and three closely related arithmetic benchmarks. GSM8K-AUG and GSM8K-AUG-NL contain the same questions and answers with differently formatted traces, so the evidence does not establish broad natural-language reasoning, long-horizon reasoning, or scaling beyond small 0.5B–3B models.

Baseline comparison is not fully controlled: several results are copied from prior papers, KAVA receives a broader hyperparameter sweep, and uncertainty is missing for many baselines and all reported Llama-3B results. No significance testing is provided despite several small differences.

The paper does not sufficiently isolate the incremental contribution of KV distillation across datasets and model sizes. The most direct removal of the KV loss appears only in a limited Llama-1B trace-processing ablation; comprehensive comparisons against the otherwise identical PCCoT/CODI training pipeline are absent.

Important technical details are ambiguous. Independent per-head/per-layer eviction eliminates cross-layer token identity, yet the ordering used for position-wise KV matching is not specified. The treatment of positional/rotary encoding when matching keys from different original positions is also unexplained. Appendix pseudocode uses pad_tokens before defining it and appears potentially to apply softmax again to already normalized attention scores.

Reproducibility is incomplete: there is no code release, exact decoding and answer-extraction protocol, hardware/training cost, sweep ranges, or seed specification. The meaning of layer-wise standardization and the precise no-projection configuration are not defined.

The interpretability analysis is anecdotal and based on a few examples. Moreover, one displayed natural-language teacher trace itself gives an incorrect intermediate/final result, weakening the conclusions drawn from decoded traces.

The paper motivates latent reasoning partly through concerns about unreliable explicit rationales but provides no substantive safety or ethics discussion concerning the reduced auditability of opaque latent reasoning.

strengths: The paper proposes an interesting and reasonably novel combination of latent reasoning, self-distillation, and redundancy/importance-aware KV-cache compression. Directly supervising latent tokens through compressed keys and values is intuitively motivated.

The method is evaluated with three backbone sizes/families, including a 3B model, and generally improves substantially over the no-CoT baseline. Several results—particularly for Qwen-0.5B and natural-language traces—are promising.
The paper includes useful component analyses covering the CODI loss, projection layer, eviction criterion, loss function, latent-token budget, and Jacobi iterations.
The presentation is generally understandable, and the paper supplies public dataset identifiers and most optimization hyperparameters.
weaknesses: The claim that KAVA consistently outperforms latent baselines is contradicted by Table 1. For example, on LLaMA-1B trained on GSM8k-AUG, CODI exceeds KAVA on GSM8k-Hard and SVAMP; on LLaMA-3B trained on natural-language traces, CODI substantially exceeds KAVA on SVAMP. Several other relevant baseline entries are missing, preventing comprehensive comparison.

Baseline comparisons are not sufficiently controlled. KAVA is selected through a multi-dimensional validation sweep and evaluated with three seeds, whereas many baselines are copied from prior papers or tuned only over learning rate. Standard errors are absent for most baselines and even for the reported 3B KAVA results, despite the stated three-seed protocol. Consequently, small gains such as 56.5 versus 55.6 cannot be interpreted confidently.

The efficiency evidence does not support the central deployment claims. Counting forward passes treats an autoregressive one-token step as comparable to a Jacobi pass over all 24 latent positions, despite different FLOPs, attention costs, memory traffic, and batching behavior. No measured latency, throughput, peak memory, KV-cache footprint, or total FLOPs is reported. Claims of 62–92% efficiency improvement are therefore potentially misleading.

Evaluation is narrow: all experiments concern elementary arithmetic word problems, with training and primary testing derived from GSM8K and only GSM8K-Hard and SVAMP used for transfer. There is no evidence for longer-horizon reasoning, non-mathematical tasks, larger reasoning models, or realistic natural-language workloads, so the broad claims about scalable latent reasoning are unsupported.

The main claimed advantage on natural-language traces is not adequately ablated. The direct controlled comparison obtained by removing the KV loss is reported only for one model on the equation-only setting. Comparable multi-seed ablations on GSM8k-AUG-NL are needed to establish that KV supervision, rather than tuning or another component, causes the claimed robustness.

Important methodological details remain unclear. Independent top-M selection for every layer and head destroys a shared token ordering, yet the paper does not explain how selected entries are ordered before index-wise matching to student positions. The projection architecture, layer-wise loss normalization, precise Jacobi implementation, and behavior of shared teacher/student parameters are also insufficiently specified.

The eviction score uses attention from ground-truth answer tokens. Although restricted to training, this is target-conditioned supervision that may preferentially encode answer information rather than a reusable reasoning trajectory. The paper neither analyzes this leakage-like shortcut nor compares against selection criteria that do not access the answer.

The interpretability evidence is anecdotal and overstated. Only three successful examples are shown, the natural-language latent readouts are largely fragmentary, and no aggregate fidelity or faithfulness measure is provided. Cosine-similarity plots are expected given the explicit matching objective and do not demonstrate that the latent trajectory implements the teacher's reasoning.

Reproducibility is incomplete: no implementation or trained models are provided, and the supplied pseudocode references `pad_tokens` before defining it. Hardware, training cost, prompt formatting, answer extraction, exact checkpoint-selection protocol, and complete seed-level results are missing.

The paper does not discuss the safety and auditability implications of replacing inspectable reasoning traces with opaque latent computation, despite motivating the work partly through reliability concerns about explicit CoT.

strengths: The core idea—using a compressed teacher KV-cache as stepwise supervision for continuous latent reasoning—is novel, intuitive, and relevant to efficient reasoning.
The method is evaluated across three backbones and two trace styles, with especially encouraging gains on several natural-language-trace settings.
The paper includes useful ablations of the KV loss, eviction rule, latent-token budget, Jacobi iterations, projection layer, and removal of the final reasoning step.
KAVA substantially reduces the reported inference-pass count relative to explicit CoT while remaining much more accurate than No-CoT.
The presentation is generally clear, with a coherent connection among latent reasoning, cache compression, and self-distillation.
weaknesses: The empirical scope is too narrow for the broad claims: all training and evaluation concern elementary arithmetic, and GSM8K-Hard and SVAMP provide limited evidence of general reasoning transfer. Scaling is demonstrated only up to 3B parameters.

The claim that KAVA consistently outperforms latent baselines is inaccurate. CODI is better on multiple reported settings, including LLaMA-1B GSM8K-Hard/SVAMP and LLaMA-3B natural-language SVAMP. Several gains are small, while uncertainty is unavailable for many baselines.

Baseline comparisons are not fully controlled: many results are copied from prior work, standard errors are reported inconsistently, and KAVA receives its own validation sweep. This makes statistical and tuning-budget comparisons difficult.

Efficiency is measured only by the number of forward passes, which is not comparable across autoregressive single-token decoding and Jacobi passes processing an entire latent block. No latency, throughput, FLOPs, peak memory, KV-cache size, or training overhead is reported, weakening the efficiency and deployability claims.

Important implementation details of KV matching are underspecified, including whether keys are taken before or after positional transformations such as RoPE and how independently selected top-M entries are ordered before index-wise matching. The appendix pseudocode also uses the padding mask before defining it and appears to apply softmax to attention scores that Equation 5 already defines as normalized.

The interpretability discussion is largely qualitative and based on selected examples rather than a systematic evaluation. Broader analyses of latent-trace faithfulness or causal relevance are missing.
Overall, this is a promising and technically interesting paper, but the limited and partially uncontrolled evaluation leaves the evidence slightly below the acceptance threshold for a top-tier venue.

strengths: The paper introduces a clear and technically interesting supervision mechanism: independently compressing the teacher’s per-layer, per-head KV cache and matching it to the student’s continuous latent trajectory. This addresses a genuine limitation of latent-reasoning methods, whose intermediate states otherwise receive little direct supervision.

The empirical study is reasonably broad, covering three model configurations from two families, equation-only and natural-language traces, several in- and out-of-distribution benchmarks, and substantially longer MetaMathQA traces. KAVA generally improves over relevant latent-reasoning baselines, with especially convincing gains for Qwen-0.5B and natural-language training traces.

The component ablations provide useful evidence that the KV objective contributes beyond the underlying PCCoT/CODI framework. The comparisons among combined, attention-only, similarity-only, and cropping-based eviction also support the proposed redundancy-and-importance-aware target construction.

The paper examines accuracy-efficiency trade-offs, latent-token and Jacobi-iteration counts, training-data scaling, trace placement, alternative teacher-generated traces, and qualitative properties of the learned representations. This is more comprehensive than a single-benchmark accuracy comparison.

The method has practical appeal because cache compression is used only to construct training targets; inference retains the compact latent-reasoning behavior without requiring an explicit teacher or online eviction procedure.
weaknesses: The reported efficiency metric is only the number of forward passes. A Jacobi pass processes all latent positions simultaneously and is not computationally equivalent to one cached autoregressive decoding step. The paper does not report latency, throughput, FLOPs, peak memory, or actual KV-cache size, so claims of 62–92% inference-efficiency improvement are not adequately established by systems measurements.

Experimental uncertainty is reported inconsistently. Several principal Qwen and Llama-3B baseline results and all Llama-3B KAVA results lack error bars, while the MetaMathQA Pareto curves report only non-diverged baseline runs without seed counts or uncertainty. This makes the reliability and significance of some gains difficult to judge.

Hyperparameter selection is asymmetric: KAVA receives sweeps over learning rate, loss coefficient, norm, and normalization, whereas new baseline runs appear to receive only learning-rate tuning or inherited hyperparameters. Combined with baseline instability and selective reporting of non-diverged runs, this leaves some concern that part of the advantage reflects tuning effort rather than the proposed objective alone.

The method description does not specify whether the independently selected top-M cache entries are restored to original sequence order or retained in score order before index-wise KV matching. Because selections differ across heads and layers, this ordering choice is important for defining the target trajectory and reproducing the method. The provided pseudocode also uses `pad_tokens` before defining it and omits the actual selection, ordering, and gathering steps.

The central evaluation remains limited to relatively small 0.5B–3B models and mostly grade-school mathematical reasoning. Moving from 1B to 3B is only modest evidence for the claimed scalability, and performance remains noticeably below full CoT in many settings. Broader reasoning domains and larger contemporary models would strengthen the significance claim.

The interpretability analysis is mostly anecdotal and potentially circular: higher similarity to the compressed teacher cache is directly optimized by the training loss, and decoded traces are shown for only a few examples. It does not establish that latent states represent faithful reasoning or explain the observed accuracy improvements.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite the paper’s claim that all necessary details are provided: no code or artifact release is identified, important implementation choices are ambiguous, and training cost and hardware are not reported. There are also presentation issues, including an ablation table visibly overlapped by plots and several notation or pseudocode errors.

strengths: The idea of using an answer-aware compressed teacher KV cache as supervision for continuous latent reasoning is interesting and reasonably novel.
The method is evaluated with three model configurations and several in-distribution and out-of-distribution arithmetic benchmarks.
The paper includes useful ablations covering eviction criteria, loss functions, loss coefficients, latent-token counts, Jacobi iterations, trace placement, and training-data size.
KAVA often improves accuracy over CODI and PCCoT, with particularly substantial gains for Qwen-0.5B and on natural-language GSM8K traces.
The manuscript is generally readable, and its main architecture and training objective are presented clearly.
weaknesses: The claimed efficiency gains are not convincingly established. Counting a Jacobi update over 24 simultaneous latent positions as one 'forward pass' and comparing it with one autoregressive token step does not measure comparable computation. The paper reports no latency, throughput, FLOPs, memory, or energy results, despite making deployability and KV-footprint claims.

Several headline claims are overstated. KAVA does not consistently outperform the latent baselines: PCCoT or CODI is better on some Llama-1B results, and CODI exceeds KAVA by four points on Llama-3B SVAMP under GSM8K-AUG-NL training. The claimed smaller degradation on natural-language traces also does not hold uniformly for Llama-3B.

The evaluation does not cleanly isolate the contribution of compressed-KV supervision. KAVA combines PCCoT-style parallel latent computation, CODI loss in most main experiments, a projection layer, and KV matching. The ablations do not provide a comprehensive, consistently configured comparison showing that KV matching itself explains the gains across models and datasets.

The positional meaning of the KV objective is under-specified. Top-M entries are selected independently for every layer and head, destroying not only token correspondence but also a coherent cross-head step ordering. Nevertheless, Equation 7 applies an index-wise loss. The paper does not specify the ordering of selected entries or whether keys are matched before or after positional/rotary encoding, making the purported 'stepwise trajectory' supervision difficult to interpret and reproduce.

The experimental protocol is inconsistent. Some entries have uncertainty estimates while all Llama-3B results and many baselines do not, despite the statement that selected settings are run with three seeds. No statistical tests are given, and several reported improvements are comparable to run-to-run variation.

The MetaMathQA comparison is vulnerable to selection bias: the authors report only non-diverged CODI and PCCoT runs, while KAVA uses a materially different objective with the CODI term removed. This prevents the Pareto curves from serving as a controlled comparison.

The appendix pseudocode is not executable as written because `pad_tokens` is used before it is defined. There is also ambiguity about whether already normalized attention probabilities are passed to the routine and softmaxed again.

The empirical scope is narrow relative to the broad claims: all tasks are arithmetic, models are at most 3B parameters, and training uses hundreds of thousands of augmented traces. There is no evidence on symbolic logic, code, science, long-horizon planning, or contemporary larger reasoning models.

The claim that the student 'directly generates the compressed KV-cache' is not demonstrated. At inference it generates ordinary latent states whose K/V tensors were encouraged to resemble selected teacher entries; the paper does not show that these caches are functionally interchangeable or causally responsible for the accuracy gains.

Reproducibility is incomplete: no code or trained artifacts are provided, baseline hyperparameters are not fully tabulated, and important details such as hardware, training cost, exact seed protocol, decoding settings, answer extraction, top-M ordering, and validation-selection budget are absent.

The interpretability analysis is largely qualitative and sometimes weakens the narrative: natural-language latent traces resist decoding, and higher similarity to the explicitly optimized eviction target is expected rather than independent evidence that reasoning knowledge was transferred.

The use of gold-answer-token attention to construct training targets is reasonable as privileged distillation information, but its role is not sufficiently analyzed. An ablation with question-only or trace-intrinsic importance is needed to determine whether gains come from compressed reasoning supervision or direct answer-conditioned target selection.

strengths: The paper presents a clear and original idea: compressing a teacher’s answer-aware KV cache and using it as stepwise supervision for continuous latent reasoning. This is a meaningful connection between KV-cache compression and latent-chain-of-thought research.

The empirical study is reasonably broad, covering three model configurations, equation-only and natural-language traces, multiple in-distribution and out-of-distribution math benchmarks, and the substantially longer MetaMathQA traces.

KAVA generally provides a favorable accuracy–computation trade-off and often substantially improves over CODI and PCCoT, with particularly convincing gains for Qwen-0.5B and on natural-language training traces.

The ablations examine the KV objective, projection layer, eviction strategy, loss design, latent-token/iteration counts, data scale, and alternative trace generators. The experiments support the conclusion that KV supervision contributes beyond the underlying PCCoT framework.
The paper is well organized, motivates the supervision problem clearly, and includes useful qualitative analysis of the relationship between student latent states and the compressed teacher cache.
weaknesses: The efficiency evidence is incomplete. The paper primarily counts forward passes, even though a parallel pass over 24 latent positions has a different cost from a single-token autoregressive pass. No wall-clock latency, throughput, FLOPs, peak memory, or actual KV-cache measurements are reported, weakening claims about deployment efficiency.

The claim that KAVA consistently outperforms the latent baselines is overstated. It is slightly behind PCCoT or CODI on some Llama-1B results and notably trails CODI on Llama-3B/SVAMP after natural-language training (66.1 versus 70.1).

Statistical reporting is uneven: uncertainty is given for many KAVA results but omitted for several baselines and all reported 3B results. Consequently, some small improvements cannot be distinguished from run-to-run variation. Only non-diverged baseline runs are reported for parts of the MetaMathQA study, which can also complicate comparison.

Baseline tuning is not fully controlled. KAVA receives a sweep over learning rate, loss coefficient, loss type, and normalization, whereas some baselines are copied from prior work or tuned only over learning rate. Differences in trace preprocessing and training stability further limit a clean attribution of gains to KV distillation.

Reproducibility is weaker than claimed: the paper provides no code-release statement, compute budget, hardware, training time, or complete hyperparameter-search ranges. The eviction pseudocode also references `pad_tokens` before defining it and appears to apply softmax to attention scores that Equation 5 already defines as softmax-normalized.

The evaluation is confined almost entirely to arithmetic word problems with small models. Broader reasoning domains and stronger modern backbones would be needed to establish that compressed KV supervision generalizes beyond this setting; the interpretability evidence is likewise mostly qualitative and anecdotal.
